section_summary: This section concerns the revival and restriction of Japanese industry during the occupation. British parliamentary debate and press clippings focus on textile exports, labour standards and reparations, while Far Eastern Commission records establish interim production capacity levels. Correspondence also addresses soda ash shortages, imports from occupied countries, and the status of a British owned mill in Japan.

subfiles.title: House of Commons oral answers on Japanese industry
subfiles.about: MPs question Stafford Cripps about Japanese textile exports, labour standards, reparations and British competition.
subfiles.summary: Cripps says Japan must export to become self supporting and that wage standards cannot presently be imposed. MPs raise concerns about Lancashire textiles, raw cotton, reparations and public ownership.

subfiles.title: Japan's Textile Exports
subfiles.about: Reports British reaction to Cripps's policy on Japanese textile exports.
subfiles.summary: An incomplete clipping reports concern about low wage competition and the lack of immediate controls on Japanese textiles.

subfiles.title: Japan's Textile Exports
subfiles.about: Reports British reaction to Cripps's policy on Japanese textile exports.
subfiles.summary: A fuller duplicate describes parliamentary concern, possible debate and objections to higher raw cotton prices.

subfiles.title: Japanese Competition
subfiles.about: Argues that Japan needs peaceful exports to pay for imports.
subfiles.summary: The editorial supports revived Japanese light industry while urging fair trade practices and gradual wage improvements.

subfiles.title: Statistical Data Relating to Interim Reparations Removal Proposals
subfiles.about: Requests US statistics on industries discussed for interim reparations removals.
subfiles.summary: Johnson seeks data for Far Eastern Commission consideration.

subfiles.title: Further request for industrial statistics
subfiles.about: Seeks statistics on seven industries requested by the Chinese commission member.
subfiles.summary: Johnson refers to the November 8 request and a list of seven industries.

subfiles.title: Referral of Johnson memorandum
subfiles.about: Directs the November 14 request to the division handling Johnson's earlier memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Routes the request for action.

subfiles.title: Referral to Fisher
subfiles.about: Forwards the statistics request for action.
subfiles.summary: Requests appropriate action and a reply through the office.

subfiles.title: Chinese request for statistical data
subfiles.about: Transmits the Chinese member's request for statistics on seven industrial categories.
subfiles.summary: The enclosure lists nitrogen fixation, pulp and paper, rayon, dyestuffs, rubber, vessels and technical research laboratories.

subfiles.title: Reply on industrial statistics
subfiles.about: Responds to requests for statistics on industries proposed for reparations removal.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring says industrial studies are being supplied, except for technical research laboratories.

subfiles.title: Instruction to answer Congressman Andrews
subfiles.about: Requests an expedited draft reply to Congressman Andrews.
subfiles.summary: Asks Lewis to prepare a letter for Hilldring's signature.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about ceramics imports
subfiles.about: Asks whether ceramics from occupied Germany and Japan enter the US duty free.
subfiles.summary: Andrews relays a constituent's concern that revived china production competes with American goods.

subfiles.title: Clearance note for Andrews reply
subfiles.about: Records clearance of the response to Andrews.
subfiles.summary: Notes consultation with Walk and Parks.

subfiles.title: Reply to Congressman Andrews
subfiles.about: Explains the policy for peaceful industry and ceramics imports from Germany and Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring says imports pay for occupied countries' needs, are subject to ordinary duties, and are sold at fair market prices.

subfiles.title: British views on Japanese industrial levels
subfiles.about: Reports preliminary British proposals for Japanese steel, shipping and labour policy.
subfiles.summary: A correspondent expects cabinet consideration of proposals to raise Japanese wages and curb textile exports.

subfiles.title: Revival of Japanese soda ash industry
subfiles.about: Proposes asking SCAP whether Japanese soda ash capacity could meet US shortages.
subfiles.summary: Whitman outlines possible private supply of raw materials in return for soda ash output.

subfiles.title: Approval request for soda ash inquiry
subfiles.about: Seeks approval to cable SCAP about Japanese soda ash capacity.
subfiles.summary: Claxton reports War Department concurrence despite likely coal shortages.

subfiles.title: War Department concurrence on soda ash inquiry
subfiles.about: Requests War Department concurrence for a cable about Japanese soda ash production.
subfiles.summary: Lewis describes the US shortage and proposes asking SCAP about usable capacity.

subfiles.title: Telephone note about soda ash letter
subfiles.about: Records discussion of Biggers's soda ash request.
subfiles.summary: Notes War Department awareness and a planned cable to SCAP.

subfiles.title: Routing of Cox correspondence
subfiles.about: Requests action on Cox's letter and a possible reply.
subfiles.summary: Suggests sending Cox a copy of Clayton's response.

subfiles.title: Cox letter forwarding Biggers request
subfiles.about: Forwards Biggers's request to increase the US soda ash supply.
subfiles.summary: Cox urges action on the shortage.

subfiles.title: Biggers proposal for soda ash imports
subfiles.about: Proposes obtaining soda ash from Germany, Japan and Italy.
subfiles.summary: Biggers describes the US shortage, recommends operating a Duisburg plant, reviving Japanese production and supplying coal to an Italian plant in exchange for output.

subfiles.title: Follow-up routing note on Cox letter
subfiles.about: Asks Claxton to follow up the Cox and Biggers letters.
subfiles.summary: Notes the original Cox letter was forwarded for action.

subfiles.title: Copy of Cox letter
subfiles.about: Duplicates Cox's forwarding letter about the soda ash shortage.
subfiles.summary: Urges action to augment US supply.

subfiles.title: Copy of Biggers proposal
subfiles.about: Duplicates the proposal for soda ash imports from Germany, Japan and Italy.
subfiles.summary: Biggers recommends maintaining German production, restoring Japanese plants and exchanging coal for additional Italian output.

subfiles.title: Instruction to answer McConaughy
subfiles.about: Requests a reply to McConaughy while Hilldring is away.
subfiles.summary: Suggests naming an available State Department contact.

subfiles.title: Referral of McConaughy inquiry
subfiles.about: Refers the McConaughy inquiry for a reply.
subfiles.summary: Requests a response along Cameron's suggested lines.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about acquisition of Japanese company
subfiles.about: Requests a meeting about occupation controls affecting a proposed acquisition.
subfiles.summary: An American client is considering acquiring a Japanese subsidiary of an affiliated British company.

subfiles.title: Reply to McConaughy
subfiles.about: Offers Whitman as a contact during Hilldring's absence.
subfiles.summary: Invites discussion of Japanese occupation controls with Whitman's staff.

subfiles.title: Revised reply to McConaughy
subfiles.about: Revises the reply offering Whitman as a State Department contact.
subfiles.summary: Provides a contact while Hilldring is away.

subfiles.title: British press treatment of Pauley's recommendations
subfiles.from: Everett F. Drumright, American Embassy London
subfiles.about: Reports limited British press coverage of Pauley's Japanese reparations proposals.
subfiles.summary: Drumright says the Manchester Guardian alone offered sustained analysis, fearing that severe restrictions would impoverish Japan and harm world trade.

subfiles.title: Another Potsdam?
subfiles.about: Criticizes Pauley's proposed restrictions on Japanese industry.
subfiles.summary: The editorial argues that removing extensive capacity in steel, machinery, shipping, soda ash and power would leave Japan unable to support its population or pay for imports. It urges the British government to state its position.

subfiles.title: Circulation of SWNCC amendments
subfiles.about: Circulates proposed amendments on advance transfers of Japanese reparations.
subfiles.summary: Requests comment or concurrence.

subfiles.title: Telephone notes on SWNCC 236/37
subfiles.about: Explains State Department objections to a War Department amendment.
subfiles.summary: Martin says SCAP's position on retention levels is unclear and the proposed amendment would prejudge industrial disarmament decisions.

subfiles.title: Request for information on Yao Mills
subfiles.about: Requests occupation authorities to report on a British owned mill in Osaka.
subfiles.summary: Seeks the mill's condition, operating status and property control status.

subfiles.title: Airgram requesting Yao Mills status
subfiles.about: Requests a cable report on Yao Mills and British ownership.
subfiles.summary: Repeats Wickersham's questions about condition, operation and custody.

subfiles.title: Follow-up telegram on Yao Mills
subfiles.about: Asks for preliminary information on Yao Mills without waiting for full details.
subfiles.summary: Expedites the February 5 inquiry.

subfiles.title: Atcheson to MacArthur on plant retention
subfiles.about: Discusses Soviet demands for Allied Council consultation on Japanese plant retention.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson objects to wording that might invite Soviet inspection or criticism, but expects a compromise to secure Far Eastern Commission approval. He also mentions disagreement over publication of a constitutional review decision.

subfiles.title: Request for agricultural reform specialists
subfiles.about: Requests four specialists to assist occupation agricultural reforms in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring seeks advisers on land tenure, rural credit, taxation and cooperatives for temporary service with SCAP.

subfiles.title: MacArthur to Atcheson
subfiles.about: Responds to Atcheson's telegram on Far Eastern Commission matters.
subfiles.summary: MacArthur refers Atcheson to another message and asks about an earlier communication.

subfiles.title: Atcheson follow-up to MacArthur
subfiles.about: Reports discussions of the plant retention issue in Washington.
subfiles.summary: Atcheson believes action is temporarily held in abeyance.

subfiles.title: FEC negotiation on Allied Council wording
subfiles.about: Reports progress on wording for Allied Council consultation.
subfiles.summary: A US compromise awaits Soviet government approval; the British delegate preferred no Council reference.

subfiles.title: Handwritten file note
subfiles.about: Contains brief, largely illegible handwriting apparently referring to an FEC paper.
subfiles.summary: The note is too fragmentary to identify further.

subfiles.title: British parliamentary answer on Japanese war industries
subfiles.about: Relays a parliamentary answer on eliminating Japanese war industries.
subfiles.summary: The answer describes halted arms production, surveys of surplus capacity and consideration of reparations and future controls.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of assured capacity directive
subfiles.about: Forwards a draft directive implementing the FEC's production capacity decision.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring requests transmission to MacArthur with the Chinese representative's statement. He also addresses press release timing and Australian concerns about Allied Council discussion.

subfiles.title: Draft directive on assured production capacity
subfiles.about: Sets interim retained capacity levels for eight Japanese industrial categories.
subfiles.summary: The directive specifies levels for machine tools, steel, thermal power, soda ash and sulphuric acid, and none for arsenals, aircraft or light metals.

subfiles.title: Chinese statement on assured capacity
subfiles.about: Records Chinese and French reservations about Japanese steel capacity.
subfiles.summary: Koo says the steel limits are high and reserves the possibility of reparations from current production. Hilldring declines to commit the US.

subfiles.title: FEC transmittal of capacity decision
subfiles.about: Transmits the unanimous FEC decision on assured Japanese production capacity.
subfiles.summary: Johnson requests implementing directives to MacArthur, transmission of the Chinese statement, and delayed publication until plants are designated.

subfiles.title: Certification of FEC policy text
subfiles.about: Certifies the attached FEC policy copy.
subfiles.summary: Confirms the text matches the official version.

subfiles.title: Assured Production Capacity Levels for Japan
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Establishes interim capacity retained from reparations removal.
subfiles.summary: The policy permits designation of usable plants within specified aggregate limits. It sets ceilings for machine tools, steel, power, soda ash, chlorine, caustic soda and sulphuric acid, with no assured capacity for arsenals, aircraft or light metals.

subfiles.title: Certification of FEC minutes excerpt
subfiles.about: Certifies the attached minutes excerpt.
subfiles.summary: Confirms the excerpt matches the original text.

subfiles.title: FEC minutes on Chinese steel reservation
subfiles.about: Records debate on Japanese steel capacity and reparations from current output.
subfiles.summary: Koo questions the steel ceiling; Naggiar concurs, while Hilldring says the US makes no commitment on reparations from current production.

subfiles.title: Preliminary report on Yao Mills
subfiles.about: Reports on the former Teikoku Seishi mill.
subfiles.summary: The mill was absorbed by Fuji Spinning, remains undamaged and operating, and its British interests are protected.

subfiles.title: Present Status of Teikoku Seishi Kabushiki Kaisha
subfiles.about: Supplies further detail on the former British owned Teikoku Seishi mill.
subfiles.summary: A Civil Property Custodian report confirms British majority ownership in 1941, amalgamation into Fuji Spinning in 1943, and the mill's excellent condition and operation. Occupation authorities protect the owners' interests without taking physical custody.
